pick.name: GitHub profile README + GitHub Releases as the public changelog
pick.what: A public <username>/<username> repo README as your developer landing page; Releases (and their Atom feeds) as the changelog for each open-core product
pick.why: Free, where developer buyers and contributors look, and Claude Code can update it from commits; releases.atom feeds can also render on your Astro site
pick.free_limits: Free; repo must be public, named exactly as your username, README.md non-empty

alts.name: Astro site /changelog + /now pages
alts.what: Changelog and metrics pages on your own domain
alts.why: Best for non-developer buyers and SEO; reuse the release notes

alts.name: Buffer queue for build-in-public posts
alts.what: Schedule weekly progress posts to LinkedIn/X
alts.why: Keeps a weekly cadence without daily effort

candidates.name: Hosted changelog SaaS (Featurebase, etc.)
candidates.verdict: Not needed at this stage; not verified

decision: Use GitHub as the source of truth (profile README, Releases), mirror it to the Astro site, and post a weekly summary via Buffer. A hosted changelog tool is unnecessary until you have customers asking for in-app announcements.
